title: Travel Planning Study
instructions: Imagine yourself in each travel scenario. We’ll give you the details you need.
Compare the alternative chatbot responses and choose the approach you would prefer. There are no right or wrong answers.
Treat every checkpoint as a fresh example. Your choices do not change what happens next.

scenarios.title: A few days in Washington, DC

introduction.text: Imagine a solo, three-night trip to Washington, DC. You’re looking forward to neighborhood walks, museums, and a little time to explore.
Your travel dates are fixed, and you have $2,400 for the trip. You’re considering how a travel assistant could help you plan.

checkpoints.title: Finding a place to stay

context.text: You need a private room for three nights. These two fictional hotels are available for your dates.

checkpoints.travelerMessage: Can you help me choose a hotel?
checkpoints.question: How would you like to approach this choice?

options.text: Here’s a comparison of price and location for both hotels. You can decide which one you’d like to add to your itinerary.
I recommend Union Hotel because it’s closer to transit. Would you like me to add it to your draft itinerary?
I’ve added Union Hotel to your draft itinerary for its convenient transit access. You can change it. Nothing has been booked.
I’d compare the hotels and make this choice myself, without chatbot assistance.

checkpoints.title: When a plan needs a rethink

context.text: In this independent example, Union Hotel was on a draft itinerary, but the room is no longer available. Nothing has been booked, and Park Hotel is still available for $600.

checkpoints.travelerMessage: The hotel is unavailable. What should we do?
checkpoints.question: Which response would you prefer now?

options.text: That room is no longer available. Would you rather keep the lower price or stay close to transit? I can look for another option based on what matters to you.
That room is no longer available. Park Hotel is still available for $600. I suggest it as an alternative. Shall I update your draft itinerary?
I’d take over the hotel search and work out an alternative myself.

introduction.text: Now imagine a different trip: a relaxed two-night visit to the coast with a friend. You’re sharing a total budget of $700.

items: You can travel on any weekend in September 2027.
You’d like time outdoors and one local activity.
Treat this as a fresh scenario, independent of your earlier choices.

checkpoints.title: Getting there together

context.text: A return train journey costs $120 for two people and takes three hours each way. A return coach journey costs $70 for two people and takes four hours each way. Both fit your possible weekends.

checkpoints.question: How much help would you like with transportation?

options.text: The coach saves $50, while the train saves an hour each way. Here are the details so you can choose the best fit.
I’ve added the coach to your draft itinerary to leave more of your budget for the weekend. You can change it. No tickets have been bought.
I’d compare transportation and choose it myself, without chatbot assistance.

checkpoints.title: Making room for a little exploring

context.text: In this independent example, your accommodation and transport are already arranged. You have $90 left for activities for both of you. A guided coastal walk costs $50 for two; exploring a public beach is free.

checkpoints.travelerMessage: Help us plan an afternoon outdoors.
checkpoints.question: Which approach would you prefer?

options.text: I suggest the guided coastal walk for $50, leaving $40 of your activity budget. Would you like to add it to the plan?
We’d decide how to spend the afternoon ourselves, without chatbot assistance.
